sources.1: Parker O-Ring Handbook ORD 5700: Design Chart 4-3 (face glands), Design Table 4-2 (static radial glands), §3.11 vacuum sealing and Table 3-20 (finish), §3.12.1 leak-rate approximation and Fig. 3-11 (Q), Table 3-24 (permeability), Figs. 2-4..2-6 (compression load). https://nfc.arizona.edu/sites/default/files/2022-02/parker_o-ring_handbook.pdf
sources.2: Lindley, P. B. (1967). Compression characteristics of laterally-unrestrained rubber O-rings. J. Inst. Rubber Ind. 1, 209-213 (F/L = d E (1.25 e^1.5 + 50 e^6)); as used in e.g. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.triboint.2019.106062
sources.3: Gent, A. N. (1958). On the relation between indentation hardness and Young's modulus. Trans. IRI 34, 46-57 (E [MPa] = 0.0981 (56 + 7.62336 S) / (0.137505 (254 - 2.54 S)))
sources.4: Marco Rubber, O-ring permeation (FKM: H2O 40e-8 std cc cm/cm2 s bar): https://www.marcorubber.com/o-ring-permeation.htm
sources.5: O'Hanlon, J. F. A User's Guide to Vacuum Technology, 3rd ed. (Wiley, 2003), Table 4.5 and App. C.5: outgassing of unbaked Al ~6e-9 and Viton A ~1e-6 Torr L/s/cm2 after 1 h; and Ch. 2-3 (viscous conductance, C = 135 d^4 p/L for air)
sources.6: Kozeny-Carman permeability k = d^2 e^3 / (180 (1-e)^2); Klinkenberg (1941) slip k_a = k (1 + b/p), b = 4 c lambda p / r with c ~ 1 (API Drilling and Production Practice, 200-213)
sources.7: Ergun minimum fluidization: U_mf = (rho_p - rho_g) g d^2 e^3 / (150 mu (1 - e)) for small particles (Kunii & Levenspiel, Fluidization Engineering, 2nd ed., Ch. 3)
sources.8: McMaster-Carr 4396K21 (3 cfm, 1e-2 Torr) and the parts in ../../mcmaster-parts.csv, read through the lab Pi 2026-11-17
sources.9: Airgas/Linde argon 5.0 (UHP) typical limits: O2 <= 1-2 ppm, H2O <= 1-3 ppm
sources.10: Sturm et al. (2004), Permeation of atmospheric gases through polymer O-rings used in flasks for air sampling, J. Geophys. Res. 109, D04309, https://doi.org/10.1029/2003JD004073: Viton O2 1.0-1.1e-15 and H2O ~220e-15 m2/(s hPa) (= 1.05e-8 and 2.2e-6 std cc cm/(cm2 s bar)); via Edison
sources.11: Lubkowitz et al. (2024): new AlSi10Mg powder 0.015 wt% moisture (Karl Fischer); Van Cauwenbergh et al. (2019): AlSi7Mg0.6 powder 45 +/- 11 ppm H, parts 13 +/- 4 ppm; via Edison, desktop-lpbf/edison/followup-sealing-o2/answer.md
sources.12: Pauzon et al. (2021), control of residual oxygen in LPBF (TruPrint 1000): a zirconia lambda probe read +50 ppm where an electrochemical cell read +700 ppm (H2 cross-sensitivity); leak-plus-outgassing drift ~1.7 ppm O2/min; via Edison
sources.13: Solid Sealing Technology, General Product Specifications: every hermetic part helium leak-tested, guaranteed < 1e-10 atm cc/s He; 'weldable feedthroughs are designed to have the adapter welded on the vacuum side of flanges or chambers'. https://www.solidsealing.com/img/documents/SST_General_Product_Specifications-406829.pdf (linked from the FA11631 page; read 2026-11-25 through the lab Pi). FA11631: 10 V, -269 to 450 C, 3500 psig, weld mount, $44 (https://www.solidsealing.com/products/1851/)
sources.14: Solid Sealing Technology NS13003, 26482 circular connectors, welding instructions: mating hardware 304 or 316; 'preferred orientation is with the weld on the vacuum side'; pulsed TIG 20-25 A, heat sinks on both sides, tack welds, segments of 3-4 s (never over 4 s), inert gas on the far side. https://www.solidsealing.com/img/resources/NS13003_887844.pdf (read 2026-11-25; SST lists no sheet for the single-lead and 4-pin weld-ins)

inventory.seal: Rod end: 316L block, the rod TIG-welded into its top; seven Solid Sealing weld-in feedthroughs TIG-welded at its 72 x 16 mm front face: 3 x FA11631 (Chromel) + 3 x FA11632 (Alumel) single-lead type K in Ø6.27 x 38 sleeves, 1 x FA10443 4-pin 16 A Cu in a Ø12.62 x 24 sleeve. The six type K sleeves sit 26 mm deep in blind bores joined to the rod bore by one Ø4 cross-drilling whose two ends are welded shut
inventory.held_by: welds (metal, glass-ceramic and welds: no elastomer)
inventory.in_model: block, rod socket, bores, cross-drilling, power pocket and channel, seven sleeves at the catalogue's diameters and lengths
inventory.note: SST guarantees < 1e-10 atm cc/s He per part [13], so the seven parts are < 7e-10, far under the 1e-4 mbar L/s budget; the welds (7 sleeves + 2 cross-drilling plugs + the rod) set the real leak rate: helium-test the welded block before the module is assembled. SST designs its weld-ins to be welded on the vacuum side [13, 14]; here the welds are at the block's outer (air) face, so each type K sleeve's annulus in its 26 mm bore is a crevice open to the chamber gas (a slow virtual leak and a moisture trap; ~13 mm3 each at 0.05 mm clearance). Ask SST about the blind-bore weld, weld access and the weld side, and follow its pulsed-TIG procedure (heat sinks, segments <= 4 s) [14]

other_leaks.src: rod end: 7 weld-in feedthroughs (SST: each < 1e-10 atm cc/s He [13]) and their welds; the potted stranded leads it replaced were 1e-5 to 1e-2
other_leaks.fix: helium-test the welded rod-end block before the module is assembled and accept < 1e-9 mbar L/s (the upper value): the welds, not the parts, set it

soft_pump.note: metering valve with Cv >= this in parallel with the KF-25 valve; open the main valve below ~100 mbar. Back-fill through the same limit (the flowmeter-regulator 78595A5 set <= 25 L/min) and a sintered diffuser

rate_of_rise.note: isolate at <= 1 mbar after >= 1 h pumping; read a Pirani or capacitance gauge for 10 min
